title: The canonical sheaf of a smooth curve
statement:
Let $C$ be a smooth connected curve over $k$ of
dimension one. Then $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$
([def-sc-kahler-differentials]) is an invertible
$\mathcal O_C$-module ([def-sc-invertible-module]), i.e. a
line bundle.

proof.text:
The assertion is Zariski-local, so we may assume
$C=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a smooth $k$-algebra of
dimension one. By the local structure of smooth algebras
(commutative algebra: a smooth $k$-algebra of dimension $n$ has a
presentation $A=k[x_1,\dots,x_{n+c}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ with Jacobian
matrix $(\partial f_i/\partial x_j)$ of rank $c$, and then

$$
\Omega^1_{A/k}=A^{\oplus(n+c)}\big/(df_1,\dots,df_c)
$$

is finite projective of rank $n$, generated by
$dx_1,\dots,dx_n$ – the Jacobian criterion), $\Omega^1_{A/k}$
is projective of rank one, hence locally free of rank one, i.e. $\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is a line bundle.

blueprint_update.statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes which is smooth of relative
dimension one, and let $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ be its sheaf of relative Kähler
differentials (defined as in [def-sc-kahler-differentials], with the
rings of sections of $\mathcal O_S$ in place of $k$). Then
$\Omega^1_{X/S}$ is an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module
([def-sc-invertible-module]). In particular, for a smooth connected
curve $C$ over $k$ of dimension one, $\omega_C=\Omega^1_{C/k}$ is a
line bundle.

proof.text:
The assertion is Zariski-local on $X$ and on $S$, so we may assume
$S=\operatorname{Spec}R$ and $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$ with $A$ a smooth
$R$-algebra of relative dimension one; then $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ is the
sheaf associated with $\Omega^1_{A/R}$. By the local structure of
smooth algebras (commutative algebra: locally, a smooth $R$-algebra of
relative dimension $n$ has a presentation
$A=R[x_1,\dots,x_{n+c}]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ with Jacobian minor
$\det(\partial f_i/\partial x_{n+j})_{i,j\le c}$ invertible in $A$, and
then

$$
\Omega^1_{A/R}=A^{\oplus(n+c)}\big/(df_1,\dots,df_c)
$$

is free of rank $n$, generated by $dx_1,\dots,dx_n$ – the Jacobian
criterion), $\Omega^1_{A/R}$ is free of rank one on a neighbourhood of
each point, i.e. $\Omega^1_{X/S}$ is invertible. For a smooth connected
curve $C$ of dimension one over $k$, $C$ is irreducible (smooth, hence
normal, and connected), so it is smooth of relative dimension one over
$\operatorname{Spec}k$, and the first part applies.
